mechanism_narrative: A high federal funds rate indicates tight monetary conditions, which may lead to decreased borrowing and spending, negatively impacting S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 60% of the 20-day windows following high FEDFUNDS levels, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate suggests labor market weakness, which may lead to decreased consumer spending and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases by >0.2pp in one month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of the 20-day windows following an unemployment rate increase, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts indicates strong demand in the housing market, which may lead to increased economic activity and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 60-day windows following an increase in housing starts, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production suggests increased economic output, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increases by >1.0pp in one month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 30% of the 20-day windows following an increase in industrial production, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising unemployment and high federal funds rates indicates stagflation, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following rising unemployment and high federal funds rates, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real consumer spending suggests strong demand, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases by >$500 million in one month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 30% of the 20-day windows following an increase in real consumer spending, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A rising federal funds rate in a tightening monetary cycle may lead to decreased liquidity and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25pp in one quarter
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of the 60-day windows following a federal funds rate increase, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in non-farm payroll employment suggests a strong labor market, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 5-day windows following an increase in non-farm payroll employment, this hypothesis is falsified.
